item.title: Uniform Resolvent Estimates for the Dunkl Laplacian
item.description: arXiv:2611.12984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let \(\Lk=-\Dk\) denote the nonnegative Dunkl Laplacian associated with a finite reflection group and a nonnegative multiplicity function \(\kappa\), and let $ N=d+2\gk\geq 3 $ be the corresponding homogeneous dimension. We establish uniform \(L_\kappa^p(\mathbb{R}^d)\)-\(L_\kappa^q(\mathbb{R}^d)\) resolvent estimates for \(\Lk\) whenever \[ \frac{2}{N+1} \leq \frac{1}{p}-\frac{1}{q} \leq \frac{2}{N}, \quad \frac{2N}{N+3}<p<\frac{2N}{N+1}, \quad \frac{2N}{N-1}<q<\frac{2N}{N-3}, \] where the last upper bound is interpreted as \(q<\infty\) when \(N=3\). Remarkably, this admissible range coincides with the corresponding range for the Euclidean Laplacian \(-\Delta\) in dimension \(N\).
item.dc:creator: Xiaofen Gao, Manli Song, Junyong Zhang

item.title: Counterexamples to the buckling eigenvalue-ratio conjecture in every dimension
item.description: arXiv:2611.13018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1999, Ashbaugh formulated the conjecture that the ball maximizes the ratio of the first two clamped buckling eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean space. We disprove this conjecture in every dimension $d\ge2$ by constructing smooth connected domains with finitely many interior holes. The key observation is that a zero-value constraint on a concentric sphere close to the boundary of a ball increases the first two eigenvalues by the same relative amount to first order, whereas their ratio increases strictly at second order. A quantitative surface penalty and logarithmic cutoffs transfer this strict inequality to smooth perforated domains. The construction gives explicit geometric parameters depending only on the dimension \(d\).
item.dc:creator: Guowei Dai, Yingxin Sun, Yong Zhang

item.title: Global regularity of axisymmetric Navier--Stokes equations under total slip and critical smallness
item.description: arXiv:2611.13263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the axisymmetric incompressible Navier--Stokes equations in a finite cylinder subject to the Navier--total--slip boundary condition, that is, the Navier slip condition with zero friction. We prove that the solution remains smooth for all time provided that the initial swirl $\Gamma_0 = r v_{\theta,0}$ has zero mean and an explicit smallness condition on the initial data holds. The condition involves $\Gamma = rv_\theta$ and the variables $V = v_\theta/\sqrt{r}$ and $\Omega = \omega_\theta/r$, and it is invariant under the natural scaling of the Navier--Stokes equations, hence critical. The total-slip condition produces a boundary term on the lateral wall that cannot be controlled by the dissipation alone; we overcome this with a sharp trace-type identity combined with a remainder controlled by $\|\Gamma\|_{L^2}$. In addition, the Robin-type boundary condition $\partial_r \Gamma = 2\Gamma$ destroys the maximum principle for $\Gamma$, and we replace it with a uniform $L^4$ bound. These estimates yield uniform $L^4$ bounds for the velocity, and regularity follows from the Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin criterion together with boundary regularity results for the Navier slip condition.
item.dc:creator: Tsz-Lik Chan

item.title: Asymptotic Stability of Moving Kinks with an Internal Mode
item.description: arXiv:2611.13279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove asymptotic stability of moving kinks for one-dimensional scalar field equations with one internal mode and no threshold resonance, under a transformed repulsivity condition introduced in Kowalczyk, Martel, Mu\~noz, and Van Den Bosch and a Fermi golden rule at the second harmonic. Near every fixed subluminal velocity, arbitrary sufficiently small perturbations in $H^1\times L^2$ converge locally in the energy space to a kink with a limiting velocity. The principal difficulty is the coupling between the damping of the internal mode and modulations: the internal oscillation enters the modulation equations quadratically, whereas the damping mechanism provides only quartic time integrability. Inspired by Martel, we derive a velocity normal form from conserved momentum and incorporate the corrected velocity into the virial functional, cancelling the quadratic modulation terms that obstruct the local energy estimates. Matrix Darboux transformations, virial identities at two spatial scales, and a localized Fermi golden rule then yield simultaneous spacetime control of the internal mode and radiation, together with convergence of the velocity. We apply our criterion to the double sine-Gordon equation and suitable perturbations of the $\phi^4$ model. Through a perturbative analysis of threshold resonances, we determine the full-space discrete spectrum and establish the absence of threshold resonances. We further verify the repulsivity of the twice-transformed potential and the Fermi golden rule.
item.dc:creator: Gong Chen, Yongming Li, Zhaojie Yang

item.title: A weak maximum principle and solvability for two-dimensional elliptic equations with $L^2$-drifts and singular zero-order coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.13362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study homogeneous Dirichlet problems for second-order linear elliptic equations in divergence form on bounded open subsets $U$ of $\mathbb R^2$. The diffusion matrix is bounded, measurable, and uniformly elliptic, and the drift belongs to $L^2(U,\mathbb R^2)$. If the zero-order coefficient $c$ belongs to $L^1(U)$ and satisfies $c\ge0$, we prove a weak maximum principle and deduce uniqueness of $H^{1,p}$-weak solutions for every $p \in (2, \infty)$. No regularity of the boundary is required for this result. The proof uses a logarithmic test function and an estimate for circular means of Sobolev functions. If, in addition, $U$ is a bounded open set with Lipschitz boundary and $c\in L^s(U)$ for some $s>1$, then for every $q\in(2, \infty)$ there exists $\varepsilon\in(0,q-2)$ such that the Dirichlet problem admits a unique $H^{1,2+\varepsilon}$-weak solution for every right-hand side in $H^{-1,q}(U)$. For existence, we use estimates for the lower-order terms, the global $H^{1,p}$-estimate for the diffusion operator, and the method of continuity. Finally, on the unit disk $B_1\subset\mathbb R^2$, we construct $c\in L^1(B_1)$ with $c \geq 0$ and $f\in C_0^\infty(B_1)$ such that the Dirichlet problem for $-\Delta u+cu=f$ has a bounded weak solution in $H^{1,2}_0(B_1)$ but no weak solution in $H^{1,p}_0(B_1)$ for any $p\in(2,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Haesung Lee

item.title: A uniqueness theorem for Allen--Cahn global minimizers asymptotic to the Simons cone
item.description: arXiv:2611.13435v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every integer $m\ge4$, we prove that the saddle-shaped solution of the Allen--Cahn equation in $\R^{2m}$ constructed by Cabr\'e and Terra \cite{CabreTerra2009} is a global minimizer. Moreover, up to sign, it is the unique global minimizer whose nodal set at infinity is a normal graph over the Simons cone with a height that decays faster than that of the Hardt--Simon leaves.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee, Lorenzo Sarnataro

item.title: Regularity Estimates for a Nonhomogeneous Free Boundary Interface Problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.13443v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we establish regularity properties for minimizers of a novel nonhomogeneous interface problem with a free boundary, formulated in Orlicz-Sobolev spaces. The nonlinear terms fulfill Lieberman-type structural assumptions with subcritical growth. The principal difficulties stem from the nonhomogeneous framework and the lack of suitable representation formulas. Our findings extend recent contributions in the field and provide new insights even in the particular case of the Laplacian. Keywords: Free Boundary Problems; Orlicz-Spaces; Nonhomogeneous Operator; Transmission Problem; Regularity.
item.dc:creator: Romildo Lima, Mayra Soares, Leandro Tavares

item.title: On the two-component $b$-family system modeling shallow-water waves of medium amplitude
item.description: arXiv:2611.13493v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formally derive a two-component $b$-family system from the full governing equations for two-dimensional water waves in the medium-amplitude regime. The system contains higher-order nonlinearities and includes a two-component Camassa-Holm type system for equatorial shallow-water waves with the Coriolis effect as a special case. We establish the local well-posedness of the Cauchy problem in $B^{s-1}_{p,r}\times B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>\max\{1+\frac1p,\frac32\}$. Using Littlewood-Paley theory and Osgood's lemma, we also prove local well-posedness in the critical Besov space $B^{\frac12}_{2,1}\times B^{\frac32}_{2,1}$. Furthermore, we derive a blow-up criterion for strong solutions. For a special choice of the parameters, we prove finite-time blow-up for a class of initial data and provide an upper bound for the maximal existence time.
item.dc:creator: Mengwen Huang, Xingxing Liu

item.title: Gradient regularity without gap conditions for parabolic double phase systems with coefficients depending only on time
item.description: arXiv:2611.13529v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study degenerate parabolic double phase systems with growth exponents $p<q$ whose modulating coefficient depends only on time. In this case, the operator on each time slice has Orlicz growth with structural constants independent of the coefficient, and the system is invariant under spatial translations. Using these features, we prove second order estimates and local bounds for the gradient when the coefficient is merely bounded and measurable, and $C^{1,\alpha}$ regularity when it is H\"older continuous in time. For weak solutions with gradients in $L^q$, these results hold without any gap condition between $p$ and $q$.
item.dc:creator: Jehan Oh

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of asymptotic traveling waves in a time-fractional bistable reaction-diffusion equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13605v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study asymptotic traveling waves for a reaction-diffusion equation with a Caputo time derivative. For general $C^1$ bistable imbalanced nonlinearities, we prove the existence of an asymptotic traveling wave connecting the two stable states. The asymptotic wave speed is unique, and the asymptotic profile is strictly increasing and unique up to translation. The proof uses continuation from a stationary front and the sliding method. For a cubic nonlinearity, we also derive an asymptotic formula for the speed near the balanced case, with an explicit leading coefficient. Finally, we perform numerical simulations to compare the speed predicted by the asymptotic formula with the front propagation speed in the original equation.
item.dc:creator: Akihiro Kitamachi, Hiroshi Ishii

item.title: Classical solvability of the Cauchy problem for multi-order time-fractional systems with full matrices of differential operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.13650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article investigates the Cauchy problem in the whole space for a system of linear time-fractional partial differential equations with an arbitrary fixed number of components and a full matrix of constant-coefficient spatial differential operators. Each component is governed by its own Caputo derivative, and no rational relation between the fractional orders is required. We assume that the diagonal spatial symbols are homogeneous, positive and elliptic, while the off-diagonal entries have strictly lower order than the diagonal operator in the corresponding column. Using spatial Fourier and temporal Laplace transforms, we construct solution operators through convergent series of time convolutions involving scalar Mittag--Leffler kernels. These series account for all coupling paths, including repeated interactions between components. A fractional Duhamel representation incorporates nonhomogeneous source terms. We establish uniform convergence on bounded frequency regions and weighted multiplier estimates by separating low and high spatial frequencies. Under suitable Sobolev regularity assumptions on the initial data and continuously differentiable source terms, we prove existence and uniqueness of a classical solution, together with continuity and regularity properties in the appropriate Sobolev spaces. The general result includes two-component systems and is illustrated by fully coupled examples.
item.dc:creator: Ravshan Ashurov, Ilyoskhuja Sulaymonov

item.title: Global existence and blow-up for a fractional wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity and strong damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.13659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies a fractional strongly damped wave equation with logarithmic nonlinearity. Based on local well-posedness of weak solutions via the Galerkin approximation, we employ the potential well theory to derive the existence of global solutions under subcritical and critical initial energy conditions. Moreover, infinite time blow-up phenomena are obtained under subcritical, critical, and arbitrarily high supercritical initial energy conditions.
item.dc:creator: Guangyang Fu, Jiang Zhou

item.title: Uniqueness and Nondegeneracy of Ground States for Critical-Hardy Fractional Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13674v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study ground states of nonlinear fractional Schr\"odinger equations with the critical Hardy potential in $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $d\geq3$. We prove the existence and qualitative properties of ground states, based on which we analyze the uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states. As a byproduct, we also investigate the optimizers of the critical Hardy--Gagliardo--Nirenberg inequality, from which a sharp Keller--Hardy--Lieb--Thirring inequality is analytically derived.
item.dc:creator: YuJin Guo, Shuang Wu, Hongfei Zhang

item.title: Mean Curvature Flow with Thermal Fluctuations in Dimensions Two and Higher
item.description:
arXiv:2611.13703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surface tension drives interfaces towards smaller area, while thermal motion produces shape fluctuations whose strength is linked to the interfacial mobility through the fluctuation--dissipation relation. These mechanisms lead to mean-curvature flow with thermal noise, whose graph formulation is known as the Kawasaki--Ohta equation. We establish global-in-time existence of energy martingale solutions to the spatially regularized Kawasaki--Ohta equation for periodic graphs in every dimension $d\geq2$, with initial data in $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$. No restriction on the noise intensity is needed for $d=2$, while a smallness condition is required for $d\geq3$. The key new challenges arise from the thermal noise, which has a $(1+|
abla u|^2)^{1/4}$-type coefficient. This coefficient gives rise to an irregular Stratonovich-to-It\^o correction term of the form $
abla u\cdot D^2u
abla u/(1+|
abla u|^2)^{3/2}$. Our main innovation is a compactness argument tailored to the structure of the correction. By combining a factorization of this term with $H^1(\mathbb T^d)$ and area estimates, we establish strong convergence of the normalized gradients and reconstruct the weighted Hessian, which allows us to define the correction at energy regularity and identify its approximation limit.
item.dc:creator: Zhengyan Wu, Ao Zhang

item.title: Local well-posedness, wave breaking and ill-posedness for the unidirectional non-local wave model
item.description: arXiv:2611.13734v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first establish local well-posedness (existence, uniqueness and continuous dependence) for the Cauchy problem associated with the unidirectional non-local wave model in the Besov spaces $B^s_{p,r}$ with $s>1+\frac{1}{p}$ and $1\leq p,r\leq\infty$, as well as in the critical Besov spaces $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,1}$ with $1\leq p<\infty$. Next, by exploiting the fine structure of the equation and performing a delicate analysis of the commutator terms, we establish a new sufficient condition for wave breaking without using any conservation law. Finally, we prove that the model is ill-posed in $B^{1+\frac{1}{p}}_{p,r}$ for $1\leq p\leq\infty$ and $1<r\leq\infty$. Our analysis further clarifies the well-posedness theory and wave-breaking behavior of the unidirectional non-local wave model arising from the motion of a cold plasma in a magnetic field, which refines and improves previously known related results.
item.dc:creator: Jian Chen, Shaojie Yang, Zhaoyang Yin

item.title: Uniqueness and nondegeneracy of ground states for the pure-power Born-Infeld equation
item.description: arXiv:2611.13735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For \(N\ge3\) and \(p>2N/(N-2)\), we study the Born--Infeld equation \[ -\diver\!\left(\frac{\nabla u}{\sqrt{1-|\nabla u|^2}}\right) =|u|^{p-2}u \qquad\text{in }\R^N . \] We prove that the positive ground state \(Q\) is unique up to translation. We also prove that the kernel of the linearized operator at \(Q\) is spanned by \(\partial_{x_1}Q,\ldots,\partial_{x_N}Q\), and determine all nonzero optimizers of the sharp Born--Infeld Sobolev inequality. To prove nondegeneracy, we first rule out nonzero radial kernel functions using the Morse index and a Wronskian identity. We then treat the angular modes by spherical harmonics. To prove uniqueness, we compare radial solutions for large \(p\), and extend the result to all \(p>2N/(N-2)\) by compactness and continuation.
item.dc:creator: Huxiao Luo

item.title: Non-existence of solutions to a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for a system of quadratic derivative nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations introduced by M. Colin and T. Colin (2004) as a model of laser-plasma interaction. Under a coefficient condition, we prove that there are initial data admitting no solution in Sobolev spaces, both on the torus and on the Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Toshiki Kondo, Mamoru Okamoto

item.title: The anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$
item.description: arXiv:2611.13745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the anisotropic De Giorgi conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$ under the limiting assumption. More precisely, every entire solution of the anisotropic Allen-Cahn equation satisfying $u_{x_4}>0$ and $u(x,x_4)\to\pm1$ as $x_4\to\pm\infty$ for each $x\in\mathbb{R}^3$ is one-dimensional. We show that every nontrivial generalized subgraph globally minimizing the anisotropic perimeter in $\mathbb{R}^4$ is a halfspace. Combining an anisotropic tilt-excess decay estimate with a Liouville argument, we then deduce one-dimensional symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Lu Chen, Jiali Lan, Haolin Liu

item.title: A remark on Liouville-type theorems for the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$ under pointwise conditions on the head pressure
item.description: arXiv:2611.13751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the stationary Navier--Stokes equations in the three-dimensional whole space and the Liouville-type problem under the condition of finite Dirichlet integral. We give a remark on the recent result by Chae [7, Theorem 1.2], in which an upper bound of the gradient of the head pressure and a lower bound of the head pressure with certain rates were assumed to prove triviality of solutions. In this paper, we extend the range of admissible rates by two different arguments. One relies on the pointwise decay of head pressure and the classical argument of Galdi [11]. The other is similar to the argument of Chae [4, 6] and is based on the maximum principle for the head pressure, the integral identity between the vorticity and the gradient of the head pressure on the upper level set of the head pressure, and the coarea formula. This also gives a more refined proof for [7, Theorem 1.2].
item.dc:creator: Hideo Kozono, Yutaka Terasawa, Yuta Wakasugi

item.title: Existence and Splitting of Dirac Points in Honeycomb Gyromagnetic Photonic Crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.13853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish the existence of Dirac cones and magnetically induced local band gaps for the transverse magnetic Maxwell system in a two-dimensional honeycomb array of circular yttrium iron garnet (YIG) cylinders. For fixed positive material parameters with nonzero permeability contrast, we prove that sufficiently small cylinders support a Dirac point in the nonmagnetic case $\kappa_g=0$: two Bloch dispersion surfaces meet at a double eigenfrequency and form a nondegenerate cone. For each fixed sufficiently small nonzero gyrotropic bias $\kappa_g$, we show that this degeneracy splits and a local band gap opens near the original Dirac point. Our approach combines a quasi-periodic layer-potential formulation with honeycomb symmetry and rigorously controlled finite-dimensional reductions. The central contribution is a unified derivation of the conical crossing and magnetic gap opening directly from the full Maxwell transmission problem, without assuming an effective discrete model. This establishes the transition from Dirac dispersion to a locally gapped spectrum in a small-inclusion regime with fixed material contrast.
item.dc:creator: Liuyi Bao, Wei Wu

item.title: P\'olya's conjecture for hyperbolic balls and Berezin--Li--Yau type inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.13910v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the strict shifted Dirichlet P\'olya inequality \[ \lambda_k(B_R)>\frac{(d-1)^2\kappa^2}{4}+4\pi^2\left(\frac{k}{\omega_d\operatorname{Vol}_\kappa(B_R)}\right)^{2/d},\qquad k\ge1, \] for every geodesic ball $B_R$ in hyperbolic space of constant sectional curvature $-\kappa^2$, in every dimension $d\ge2$. As a consequence, we obtain the shifted Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality for hyperbolic balls, thereby providing a concrete family of domains satisfying both conjectures proposed by Laptev in 2023. For arbitrary nonempty open subsets $\Omega\subset\mathbb{H}^d_\kappa$ of finite volume, we establish the weak Berezin--Li--Yau type inequality \[ \sum_{j=1}^{m}\lambda_j(\Omega)\ge a_{d,\kappa}m+\frac{d}{d+2}\,4\pi^2\left(\frac{m}{\omega_d\operatorname{Vol}_\kappa(\Omega)}\right)^{2/d}m,\qquad m\ge1, \] with the optimal leading coefficient, where $a_{2,\kappa}=\kappa^2/4$ and $a_{d,\kappa}=d(d-1)\kappa^2/6$ for $d\ge3$. We also establish the global two-sided estimate for the renormalized eigenvalue sum on hyperbolic space, originally proposed by Strichartz in 1996 and valid for $d\ge3$.
item.dc:creator: Guowei Dai, Lan Zhao

item.title: Phase transitions and sharp localisation in anomalous localised resonance
item.description: arXiv:2611.13936v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study how detuning and absorption determine the strength and spatial extent of anomalous localised resonance in a two-dimensional quasistatic coated structure with shell permittivity $-1+c\ell^p+i\ell$, where $\ell>0$ is the loss and $c\ne0$, $p>0$ are fixed. Detuning can carry the material path through narrow resonances, producing intermittent rather than sustained power growth. For an explicit family of noncircular shells and a smooth exterior dipole source, both fixed, we classify the dissipated power under a quantitative smallness condition on the deformation. Depending on the detuning exponent and conformal source distance, the power diverges along the entire path, exhibits divergent peaks with vanishing gaps, or decays, including the threshold cases. We also identify the sharp conformal boundary beyond which the field, normalized by the square root of the dissipated power, converges locally to zero along every divergent-power sequence. For resonant sources, tangential reference crossings yield an explicit nonzero limit for the exterior gradient energy divided by the dissipated power at the critical radius.
item.dc:creator: Konstantinos Alexopoulos

item.title: A Kato-Type Criterion for Vanishing Viscosity and Magnetic Diffusivity Limits for Compressible Magnetohydrodynamics
item.description: arXiv:2611.14096v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the vanishing viscosity and magnetic diffusivity limits for the compressible magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) equations on a smooth bounded domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Under the assumptions of interior regularity and uniform local boundedness near the boundary, we establish a Kato-type criterion under which finite energy weak solutions to the dissipative MHD system converge to weak solutions to the ideal MHD system as the viscosity and magnetic resistivity coefficients decrease to zero. In particular, under such criterion, the anomalous energy dissipation in the vanishing viscosity and diffusivity limits for MHD is precluded.
item.dc:creator: Siran Li, Tong Tang, Yuanjing Tang

item.title: Sharp asymptotic stability of the incompressible porous medium equation on the whole plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.14130v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic stability of the steady state $e_s(x)=-x_2$ of the incompressible porous media equation in $\mathbb R^2$. For every $s>2$, we prove that sufficiently small initial perturbations $\theta_0\in H^s(\mathbb R^2)$ of $e_s$ generate unique global solutions $\rho=e_s+\theta$, where $\theta$ remains uniformly bounded in $H^s$ and converges strongly to zero in $H^s$ as $t\to\infty$. The main innovations of this work are threefold. First, exploiting the structure of the equation, we construct a weighted energy that eliminates the need to control $\|\nabla u^2\|_{L^1_tL^\infty_x}$. Second, rather than estimating the anisotropic commutators directly, we study the integral terms containing these commutators and establish suitable bounds through refined computations in frequency space. Third, we establish convergence in the highest-order $H^s$ norm under uniform energy bounds involving only an $L^\infty_tH^s_x$ bound on $\theta$ and an $L^2_tH^s_x$ bound on $\mathcal R_1\theta$.
item.dc:creator: Sai Li, Yang Li

item.title: Mesoscopic derivation of predator-prey dynamics via diffusive fast-reaction asymptotics: cross-diffusion and fear effects
item.description: arXiv:2611.14132v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a kinetic derivation of a spatial predator-prey model with cross-diffusion interactions and a Beddington-DeAngelis functional response. At the mesoscopic level, we divide the two populations into distinct behavioral states: prey can be active or hidden in a refuge, while predators can be either searching or handling. The microscopic state of each subpopulation is described in terms of group size and a continuous directional velocity variable, with state transitions governed by suitable Boltzmann-type interaction operators. By combining a diffusive scaling with a slow-fast formulation of the kinetic reaction operators, we formally derive a macroscopic reaction-cross-diffusion system for the total population densities of prey and predators. The limiting model consistently recovers the Beddington-DeAngelis functional response along with its associated nonlinear diffusion terms. Crucially, the kinetic upscaling yields a predator-dependent prey growth term taking a logistic form with an effective carrying capacity. This carrying capacity depends non-monotonically on predator density because prey redistribute between active and refuge states. Since density-dependent competition acts separately within these behavioral states, intermediate predator levels reduce aggregate crowding and thereby increase the effective carrying capacity of the total prey population. Overall, our derivation provides a mechanistic link connecting predator-induced behavioral shifts, refuge use, and macroscopic cross-diffusion.
item.dc:creator: Marzia Bisi, Andrea Bondesan, Maria Groppi, Cinzia Soresina

item.title: A new notion of Dirichlet boundary condition for elliptic equation of divergence form
item.description: arXiv:2611.14138v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider Dirichlet boundary conditions for elliptic equations in divergence form on rough domains by introducing a truncation-based weak solution framework that circumvents global Sobolev trace obstacles. We establish well-posedness on bounded admissible domains for continuous boundary data and $L^2$ sources, deriving boundary H\"older regularities that require only uniform ellipticity and an exterior measure-density condition. This approach eliminates the uniform domain regularity and coefficient continuity imnposed in Guam, Wang and Zhou(2026). Furthermore, on sufficiently flat Reifenberg domains, we obtain boundary $C^\alpha $ regularity for any $\alpha\in (0,1) $ using natural energy estimates, thereby bypassing $L^p$($p>\frac {n}{2}$) restrictions found in Lian and Zhang(2026). Crucially, we obtain global $H^1$ regularity for H\"older boundary data ($\alpha>\frac 12$) a posteriori, without requiring small-BMO coefficient assumptions on the coefficients.
item.dc:creator: Tianyu Guan, Lihe Wang, Chunqin Zhou

item.title: Critical Well-Posedness of a Euler-Chemotaxis System in 2D
item.description: arXiv:2611.14148v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This article is about well-posedness results for a 2D Euler-Chemotaxis-Consumption system with initial data in scale critical spaces, namely existence, uniqueness and critical initial data to solution continuity. This problem is related to the well-known family of Keller-Segel equations, although it bears major differences which will be crucial for our study. In most recent results, solutions to such Chemotaxis-Consumption systems have used a free-energy balance law to obtain well-posedness. This has the disadvantage of requiring initial data to be positive almost everywhere. Our main goal, in addition to sharp well-posedness, is to show that this positivity condition is not needed for existence and uniqueness. In fact, we will never use the concept of free-energy in our proof. Our argument revolves around an understanding of the scaling of the different parts of the equation, and especially the subcritical interaction terms. This will allow us to upgrade basic low regularity estimates (e.g. mass conservation) into critical bounds. In the process, we find out that closing $L^2$ estimates leads to the Besov space $\dot B^0_{\infty, 2}$ as the most natural choice of regularity for the initial chemo-attractant concentration. Extensive use of real interpolation also plays a key role for deriving Chemin-Lerner bounds for the solutions.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Cobb

item.title: Uniqueness of global weak solutions for the defocusing energy-critical NLS
item.description: arXiv:2611.14175v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the defocusing energy-critical nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger equation and establish global uniqueness for weak solutions. The key idea comes from the weak uniqueness in the uniform-in-time high-frequency threshold (UTHT) class introduced in [12,14]. We derive a new energy defect threshold (EDT) criterion from the UTHT criterion. Along the strong solution flow, energy conservation propagates the EDT condition for weak solutions and, combined with the global well-posedness theory for strong solutions, yields global weak uniqueness. As an application, we prove unconditional uniqueness for the quintic defocusing energy-critical Gross-Pitaevskii hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Xuwen Chen, Justin Holmer, Shunlin Shen

item.title: A stochastic chemical system in contact with reservoirs
item.description: arXiv:2611.14192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we analyse the behaviour of a non-reversible stochastic chemical system obtained as an approximation of a stochastic chemical system in which the concentration of some chemicals is higher than the concentration of the other chemicals. The master equation associated with this approximated system is characterised by a discrete part, modelling the reactions among chemicals that have low concentration, by a transport term and a diffusion term. The transport-diffusion terms describe the fluctuations in the concentration of abundant chemicals. The model contains a second order term is of order {\epsilon}, that describes the fluctuation in the concentrations of the abundand substances. We prove that the master equation has a spectral gap that is independent on $\epsilon$ and we analyse in detail the asymptotics of the solution to the master equation as $\epsilon \to 0$.
item.dc:creator: Eugenia Franco, Jann Hendrik Schr\"oders, Juan J. L. Vel\'azquez

item.title: Scattering of water waves in presence of a partially immersed obstacle
item.description: arXiv:2611.14215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study linear water waves in two dimensions in a fluid of infinite depth containing a fixed, partially immersed obstacle. Under natural geometric assumptions on the wetted boundary, we construct the harmonic lifting and prove that the associated Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator is an unbounded, self-adjoint and non-negative operator on a $L^2$ space. This yields global well-posedness and conservation of energy. We establish the absence of trapped modes and, by a compact perturbation argument, a limiting absorption principle at every positive spectral parameter. Consequently, for all finite energy initial data, the physical local energy tends to zero as $|t|\to\infty$, including in neighborhoods of the obstacle and the contact points. Quantitative resolvent estimates and fractional regularity in the spectral parameter yield algebraic local energy decay for Sobolev initial data in weighted $L^2$ spaces.
item.dc:creator: Debayan Maity, Vicente Ocqueteau, Marius Tucsnak

item.title: Global existence and sharp decay rates of weak solutions for the 2D inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress tensor diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.14228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is devoted to the global existence and optimal decay rates of weak solutions to a two-dimensional inviscid Oldroyd-B model with fractional stress diffusion. For $\frac{1}{2}<\beta<1$, by virtue of energy estimates and compactness arguments, we establish the existence of global weak solutions with $(u,\tau)\in H^{1}\times (H^{1}\cap L^{\infty})$. Moreover, based on the Littlewood-Paley decomposition theory and the improved Fourier splitting method, we derive the optimal decay rates. In particular, by constructing a suitable low-frequency energy functional and exploiting the dissipation mechanism of the coupled system, we obtain the optimal $L^\infty$ decay rate for the stress tensor.
item.dc:creator: Chen Liang, Zhaonan Luo

item.title: Generic singularity formation in two-dimensional Keller-Segel systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.14237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On bounded domains, the mass-conserving parabolic-elliptic Keller-Segel system admits smooth equilibria at every mass. Nevertheless, we prove that on a disk, an open dense set of positive initial densities leads to finite-time blow-up or infinite-time grow-up whenever the effective mass is at least the critical value $4\pi$. This threshold is sharp: below $4\pi$, every solution exists globally, remains uniformly bounded, and converges to a smooth equilibrium. At the critical mass, all solutions are global, while infinite-time grow-up accompanied by boundary concentration is generic. We extend the result to other bounded planar domains and closed surfaces, obtaining sharp mass thresholds for the round sphere and the flat square torus.
item.dc:creator: Beomjun Choi, Geuntaek Seo

item.title: Regularity via subequations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Is there a unified theory of a priori estimates for purely second-order constant coefficient elliptic PDE? A strong indication that such a theory exists is provided by the foundational a priori estimates of Caffarelli--Nirenberg--Spruck (1984) and Trudinger (1995) that treated many equations, yet left out many others. This article develops such a unified theory based on Harvey--Lawson's theory of subequations, the aforementioned a priori estimates, and some new ingredients. Serendipitously, this also solves a problem posed by Nirenberg (2007). In addition to unifying all previously known such estimates, we find a vast number of new a priori estimates (e.g., spanning real, complex, quaternionic, $G_2$, among other natural equations, and even differential inclusions that generalize PDEs).
item.dc:creator: Vasanth Pidaparthy, Yanir A. Rubinstein

item.title: Geodesically Semiconvex Approximations in the Wasserstein Space and Applications to Flow Interchange
item.description: arXiv:2611.14273v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the approximation of functionals by geodesically semiconvex functionals in the Wasserstein space, with applications to dissipation estimates along the Jordan-Kinderlehrer-Otto (JKO) scheme. For the potential and interaction energies, the approximation problem reduces to approximate the underlying potentials in Euclidean space. For the internal energies, we construct approximations by decomposing truncated functionals into differences of geodesically convex functionals and applying Moreau-Yosida regularization to the second component. Under suitable assumptions, we establish strong quantitative convergence of the gradient of the first variation in weighted \(L^2\) space. These approximations may enable us to obtain dissipation estimates along the JKO scheme for functionals that are not geodesically semiconvex. We illustrate this approach by deriving an \(L^{m+1}\) bound for the JKO scheme of fast diffusion equation, and by establishing internal energy dissipation for the JKO scheme of Fokker-Planck equation.
item.dc:creator: Kexin Lin

item.title: A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System
item.description: arXiv:2611.14315v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lema\^{i}tre--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.
item.dc:creator: Xueyi Yu

item.title: Pseudoconformal characterizations of scattering in weighted Sobolev spaces for non-scaling-invariant mass-subcritical NLS
item.description: arXiv:2611.14390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider mass-subcritical nonlinear Schr\"odinger equations with finitely many power-type nonlinearities and initial data in weighted Sobolev spaces. In the short-range regime, we prove a pseudoconformal characterization of scattering in the weighted energy space $\Sigma$. We also establish a fractional counterpart in $\Sigma^s$, $s\in(0,1)$, formulated in terms of the boundedness of the order-$s$ pseudoconformal operator. Our results include equations with combined nonlinearities, for which no distinguished scaling symmetry is available. As an application of the fractional theory, we prove small-data scattering in $\Sigma^s$, $s\in(0,1]$. The arguments rely on the lens transformation, harmonic-oscillator Strichartz estimates, and fractional harmonic Sobolev estimates.
item.dc:creator: Jacopo Bellazzini, Luigi Forcella, Vladimir Georgiev, Nicola Visciglia

item.title: Phragm\'en-Lindel\"of theorems for parabolic equations of p-laplacian-type
item.description: arXiv:2611.14392v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider rigidity properties of ancient solutions to parabolic equations of $p$-Laplacian-type. We start with the degenerate range $p>2$. First, a solution which is bounded above in an intrinsic backward paraboloid is either bounded in an entire half-space, or grows in space at least like a power with a sharp, explicit exponent. This relies on the expansion of positivity and on the Comparison Principle. Then, we turn to the growth in time. Positivity in the paraboloid alone yields no upper rate: we present explicit self-similar solutions, positive in the paraboloid, with $u(0,-T)\simeq T^{\beta}$ for every $\beta\le0$ and every $\beta\ge1$. For solutions bounded below in the paraboloid, we prove a dichotomy for the infimum of $u(\cdot,-T)$ on a ball whose radius is a fixed fraction of that of the paraboloid at time $-T$: either it is of order $T$ along a sequence of times, or it grows sublinearly, like $T^{\zeta}$ with $\zeta<1$ explicit. In the second case, a Harnack-type argument shows that the supremum on the same ball grows at most linearly. Then, we carry out the same program in the singular, supercritical range $\frac{2N}{N+1}<p<2$, where the picture is similar but several roles are reversed. In space, the iteration via the Comparison Principle can only be started from a point lying above an explicit slope, and explicit solutions show that nothing better than a cone bound can be expected below it. The self-similar profiles are unique but only local, and positivity in the paraboloid is compatible with every exponent $\beta\le1$ and with no exponent in $(1,\frac1{2-p})$. In time, the dichotomy is replaced by an a priori linear bound for the infimum. Similarities and differences between the two ranges are collected at the end of the work.
item.dc:creator: Enrico Zani

item.title: Scattering thresholds for the NLS equation with polynomially decaying damping
item.description: arXiv:2611.14403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the focusing nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with a linear damping of strength $a(1+t)^{-\theta}$, where $a>0$ and $\theta\ge0$, in the whole energy-subcritical range. For $\theta>0$, the time-averaged damping vanishes, so that the scattering theory developed in our previous work does not apply. We show that the long-time dynamics is governed by the time integrability of an effective coupling, which decays faster than any power when $\theta<1$, polynomially when $\theta=1$, and not at all when $\theta>1$. In the mass-subcritical case, all solutions are global. They scatter when $\theta<1$ and, for $\theta=1$, above an explicit exponent depending on $a$. On the other hand, no non-trivial solution is asymptotically free below a second explicit exponent when $\theta=1$, and below the short-range exponent $1+2/N$ when $\theta>1$. In the mass-critical case, solutions are global below the ground state. Moreover, for $\theta\le1$, every solution which survives until its decaying mass becomes subcritical is global and scatters. In the intercritical case, we prove small data scattering and, for $\theta\le1$, a dichotomy between scattering and grow-up of the gradient. Finally, in the scale-invariant case $\theta=1$, we analyze the range between the two thresholds. We reduce the equation exactly to a nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation with a decaying repulsive harmonic potential, and we construct approximate solitary waves with an integrable error. This leads to a conjecture, supported by numerical simulations, on the sharpness of the scattering threshold.
item.dc:creator: Makram Hamouda, Mohamed Majdoub

item.title: Sharp regularity results for variational integrals asymptotic to the $p$-Dirichlet integral
item.description: arXiv:2611.14442v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the regularity for minimisers of $\int_\Omega F(Du) \mathrm{d}x$ where $F(z) \approx |z|^p$ in suitable senses at infinity. Depending on the strength of this asymptotic condition, we discuss various regularity results, and by means of counterexamples we show they are sharp. An effort is made to obtain results without assuming unnecessary regularity of $F$ while covering the full range $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Aidan Strong

item.title: Regularity of minimisers for the $p$-distance functional
item.description: arXiv:2611.14450v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider regularity of minimisers of the $p$-distance functional $\mathcal{F}[u]=\int_\Omega \mathrm{dist}(Du,K)^p \mathrm{d}x$ where $K \subset \mathbb{R}^{N \times n}$ is a compact set. We distinguish the scalar and vectorial cases, and consider geometric conditions on $K$ where regularity can be improved.
item.dc:creator: Aidan Strong

item.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
item.description: arXiv:2611.14468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. The same pair determines the principal eigenvalue whose sign governs persistence, so early prevalence can inform the threshold even when the individual rates remain uncertain. We prove global weak well-posedness and quantitative parameter stability for the SIS system and use the resulting observation-map estimates to establish Bayesian well-posedness. For an initial infection of size $\varepsilon$, we derive a uniform second-order expansion that describes how the separate rates enter prevalence. Incidence depends explicitly on transmission at leading order. When the noise standard deviation is proportional to $\varepsilon$, we prove $O(\varepsilon)$ convergence in Hellinger distance of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits for both prevalence alone and joint prevalence and incidence data. We bound the principal eigenvalue using the growth rate of the infected $L^2$ norm between two times. This rate gives a lower bound for the full nonlinear system, and the upper bound separates spatial transients from nonlinear saturation. Uniform spectral estimates and bounds on infection size and measurement error give sufficient conditions for persistence and extinction. We also bound the error in posterior persistence probabilities under forward and eigenvalue approximation, accounting for posterior mass near the threshold. Numerical examples illustrate threshold inference and the predicted \(O(\varepsilon)\) convergence of the nonlinear posteriors to their low-prevalence limits in Hellinger distance.
item.dc:creator: Duc-Lam Duong

item.title: Non-local phase transition models for partial singularities
item.description: arXiv:2611.14478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $\Gamma$-convergence, under appropriate scalings, of the energy functionals \[ F_\varepsilon(u) := [u]_{H^s(Q)}^2 + \int_{Q} W_\varepsilon(u)\,dx, \] where $s \in (0,1)$, $[\cdot]_{H^s(Q)}$ denotes the $H^s$-seminorm in $Q\subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$, and $W_\varepsilon$ is a multi-well potential featuring infinitely many equally spaced wells together with additional intermediate wells whose height vanishes at a prescribed rate. Depending on this rate, different limiting behaviors emerge, ranging from classical models to new intermediate regimes.
item.dc:creator: Adriana Garroni, Maria Antonietta Palladino

item.title: Dynamic linear equations in the presence of small perturbations of an interface
item.description: arXiv:2611.14494v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider solutions to the initial boundary value problems for both heat and wave equations in two dimensions. In this paper, we aim to advance the development of high-order terms in the asymptotic expansions of current boundary perturbations caused by small perturbations of the shape of a $C^2$-boundary inhomogeneity. Our derivations are rigorously derived by the field expansion (FE) method (formal derivation) and proved by layer potential techniques. It extends those already derived for small-volume inhomogeneities to develop efficient algorithms for determining certain properties of the shape of an inhomogeneity based on boundary measurements.
item.dc:creator: Christian Daveau, Abdessatar Khelifi

item.title: Gradient Estimates for Singular-Degenerate Elliptic Equations with Solution-Dependent Coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.14510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a conormal boundary value problem for a class of singular-degenerate quasilinear elliptic equations in divergence form in bounded domains. The leading terms are measurable in the spatial variable and depend nonlinearly on both the solution and its gradient. The singularity or degeneracy is governed by a power of the distance to the domain boundary, with exponent greater than negative one. In particular, the corresponding weights need not belong to the Muckenhoupt $A_2$ class. Assuming that the weighted mean oscillations of the leading terms in the spatial variable are sufficiently small on small balls and that the domains have Lipschitz boundaries with sufficiently small Lipschitz constants, we establish global weighted $W^{1,p}$-estimates for weak solutions with bounded weighted mean oscillation. Our results extend recent estimates for equations whose leading terms are independent of the solution itself.
item.dc:creator: Van Le, Tuoc Phan

item.title: Microscopic derivation of the classical KMS condition for one-dimensional Bose gases
item.description: arXiv:2611.13124v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Kubo--Martin--Schwinger (KMS) condition provides an intrinsic characterization of thermal equilibrium, both in quantum and classical statistical mechanics. In this work, we establish stability of the KMS condition through the quantum-to-classical limit for one-dimensional defocusing Bose gases. More precisely, we consider scaled quantum KMS states in the (mean-field) semiclassical regime and prove that every associated Wigner measure satisfies the classical KMS condition corresponding to the nonlinear Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. This result extends to an infinite-dimensional setting an earlier derivation of the classical KMS condition for finite-dimensional Bose--Hubbard systems. It also provides a complementary perspective on the derivation of nonlinear Gibbs measures from many-body quantum statistical mechanics.
item.dc:creator: Zied Ammari, Shahnaz Farhat, S\"oren Petrat, Andrew Rout

item.title: Neumann Series of Bessel Functions for a Quadratic Sturm--Liouville Pencil
item.description: arXiv:2611.13419v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct Neumann series of Bessel functions representations for solutions and their first derivatives of the equation $-y^{\prime\prime}(x)+(q(x)+2\rho p(x))y(x)=\rho^2y(x)$. The series arise from Legendre expansions of two transmutation operator kernels. The obtained series converge uniformly on horizontal strips in the complex plane of the parameter $\rho$. We develop a recursive integration procedure for computing the coefficients of these representations. The knowledge of the first coefficients allows one to recover the potentials $p$ and $q$ which is useful for solving inverse problems. For separated boundary conditions, we estimate the characteristic functions whose zeros determine the eigenvalues. Two numerical examples illustrate the practical applicability of the obtained series representations to the solution of spectral problems.
item.dc:creator: Vladislav V. Kravchenko, Sergii M. Torba

item.title: Connectivity and the equilibration of Boltzmann-type equations on dense graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.13908v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the equilibration of solutions to a homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation whose collision kernel is given by a graphon encoding the connectivity structure of interacting agents. For a broad class of Lipschitz-continuous binary interaction rules, we show that, under suitable conditions relating the interaction parameters to the connectivity properties of the graphon, solutions converge exponentially fast towards those of the classical homogeneous Boltzmann-type equation without preferential connections, and hence towards its equilibrium distributions. We then consider in detail compromise-diffusion interaction rules and establish a quasi-invariant limit leading to a Fokker-Planck-type equation parametrised by the graphon connectivity. This limiting equation allows us to characterise explicitly both connectivity-independent and connectivity-dependent equilibrium distributions.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Tosin

item.title: On Monotonicity in Mean Field Games Induced by Discount Factor Transformations
item.description: arXiv:2611.13939v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper is devoted to the well-posedness of a class of infinite horizon discounted Mean Field Games (MFGs) problems, where both an exponential discount and a so-called cheap control factors are present simultaneously, and scale in a possibly different way. We introduce a new class of transformations of variables, at the level of both the MFG PDE and the corresponding FBSDE systems. We then show how these transformations reveal a new mechanism that generates semiconvexity estimates for the value function and ensures the existence of mean field equilibria, as long as the parameters land in a suitable regime, that we quantitatively describe. This new mechanism demonstrates furthermore how discount factors lead to a source of strong displacement monotonicity for the Lagrangian, without any initial monotonicity assumptions on the running costs. Consequently, in such regimes of parameters uniqueness of solutions manifests. Our approach uses a Lagrangian point of view, which lets us treat general non-separable Lagrangians and both deterministic and idiosyncratic noise driven models in a transparent, unified way. For a specific class of quadratic Lagrangians, using turnpike-type methods, we further obtain an exponential contractivity estimate for the mean field equilibria.
item.dc:creator: Elisa Continelli, Nicol\`o De Bernardi, Hei Jie Lam, Alp\'ar R. M\'esz\'aros

item.title: Energy Dissipation Along Trajectories and Wasserstein Gradient Flow of Aggregation-Diffusion Equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.14054v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this work, we established the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of nonlinear Fokker-Planck equations on bounded domains involving both nonlinear diffusion and nonlocal interaction effects. Our approach is based on stochastic analysis. More precisely, we investigated the associated stochastic differential equation (SDE) with normal reflection at the boundary from a trajectorial perspective and derived a semimartingale decomposition of the corresponding energy process. This decomposition leads to a trajectorial energy dissipation identity, which, together with the characterization of the metric derivative, allows us to establish the Wasserstein gradient flow structure of the aggregation-diffusion equation.
item.dc:creator: Honglei Chen, Xuewei Wang

item.title: From Distribution of Extremes With Degradation to the Stress Redundancy Principle
item.description: arXiv:2611.14375v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How a degradation source affects the statistics of the first among many identical independent stochastic particles to successfully reach a narrow target remains unclear. Here, we investigate the impact of degradation on the distributions of first-passage times and exit locations by exploiting the time-dependent fluxes associated with the corresponding Fokker-Planck equation. We also compute the escape probability by solving a mixed boundary value problem. In the large initial population $N_0$ limit, we derive an asymptotic formula for the mean first passage time associated with the fastest particle, revealing how the killing field modifies the classical $1/\log(N_0)$ scaling. However, when considering the population size at the time of the first exit, we obtain a specific dependency with respect to degradation, a phenomenon that we call the stress redundancy principle. For a degradation field restricted to a narrow subregion, we use an optimal control approach to derive the optimal trajectory where the fastest escape particles will be concentrated: interestingly, we report here that the optimal trajectories avoid the degradation area depending on killing intensity. Finally, we obtain analytical expressions for the distribution of first exit points along a narrow absorbing arc in two-dimensional regular domains. In addition, for a killing subregion tangent to the target boundary, our computations reveal how geometrical parameters influence the exit distribution. In summary, a killing source can significantly affect the statistics of the fastest diffusing particles, relevant for defining cellular and molecular time scales.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Paquin-Lefebvre, \'Elisa Delbreil, David Holcman

item.title: Regularity of $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic functions with applications to stable minimal hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.14409v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that the derivative of a $Q$-valued $C^1$ function on an $n$-dimensional domain that is locally harmonic on its regular set is locally Dirichlet minimising, and that its branch set coincides with that of its derivative. As a consequence, we get that a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is $C^{1,\alpha}$ and that its branch set is countably $(n-2)$-rectifiable when $n\geq 3$ and discrete when $n=2$. Our methods are directly applicable to the regularity theory of stable minimal hypersurfaces. We show that a multi-valued Lipschitz function whose graph is a two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal $n$-dimensional hypersurface with locally $\mathcal{H}^{n-2}$-finite singular set, and whose Lipschitz constant is sufficiently small is in fact multi-valued $C^{1,\alpha}$. As a consequence, we obtain optimal regularity conclusions for a branched sheeting theorem of Bellettini for singular immersions. When $n=2$, we obtain stronger conclusions and show that locally about a branch point, a $Q$-valued $C^1$ harmonic function is the real part of a Dirichlet minimiser which is itself obtained from a finite number of holomorphic functions via classical branching, thus giving a full series expansion for the function near the branch point. Furthermore, we prove that the class of branched, two-sided, properly immersed, stable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities is compact under varifold convergence.
item.dc:creator: Sidney Stanbury

item.title: Reverse inequality for the Riesz transforms on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2209.05083v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold satisfying the doubling volume condition for geodesic balls and L^q scaled Poincar{\'e} inequalities on suitable remote balls for some q<2. We prove the inequality $||\Delta^{1/2}f||\_p\lesssim ||\nabla f||\_p$ for all p $\in$ (q, 2], which generalizes previous results due to Auscher and Coulhon. Our conclusion applies, in particular, when M has a finite number of Euclidean ends. The proof strongly relies on Hardy inequalities, which are also new in this context and of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Baptiste Devyver (IF), Emmanuel Russ (I2M)

item.title: Logarithmic gradient estimate and Universal bounds for semilinear elliptic equations revisited
item.description: arXiv:2308.14026v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive the complete and optimal Cheng--Yau gradient estimates and universal bounds for subcritical semilinear elliptic equations on Riemannian manifolds with (Bakry-\'{E}mery) Ricci curvature bounded below. This answers a fundamental question that has existed for a long time. As a corollary, this provides a new proof of the Gidas-Spruck classical Liouville theorem. The Harnack inequality is also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Zhihao Lu

item.title: The Landau equation in a domain
item.description: arXiv:2407.09031v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This work deals with the Landau equation in a bounded domain with the Maxwell reflection condition on the boundary for any (possibly smoothly position dependent) accommodation coefficient and for the full range of interaction potentials, including the Coulomb case. We establish the global existence and a constructive asymptotic decay of solutions in a close-to-equilibrium regime. This is the first existence result for a Maxwell reflection condition on the boundary and that generalizes the similar results established for the Landau equation for other geometries in \cite{GuoLandau1,GS1,GS2,MR3625186,MR4076068}. We also answer to Villani's program \cite{MR2116276,MR2407976} about constructive accurate rate of convergence to the equilibrium {(quantitative H-Theorem)} for solutions to collisional kinetic equations satisfying a priori uniform bounds. The proofs rely on the study of a suitably linear problem for which we prove that the associated operator is hypocoercive, the associated semigroup is ultracontractive, and finally that it is asymptotically stable in many weighted $L^\infty$ spaces.
item.dc:creator: Kleber Carrapatoso, St\'ephane Mischler

item.title: Uniform dispersive estimates for the semi-classical Hartree equation with long-range interaction
item.description: arXiv:2507.12577v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we consider the Hartree equation with smooth but long-range interaction in the semi-classical regime, in three-dimensional space. We show that the density function of a small-data solution decays at the optimal rate. When the semi-classical parameter $\hbar \in (0,1]$ is fixed, our result is essentially covered by the recent work by Nguyen and You; however, the novelty of this paper is the uniformity with respect to $\hbar$. Namely, both the smallness condition for the initial data and the bounds for the solution are independent of $\hbar$. Our proof relies on three main ingredients. First, we prove the boundedness of finite-time wave operators modified by phase corrections. Second, we show an $L^1$--$L^\infty$ dispersive estimate for the modified propagator. Third, we give various kinds of commutator estimates for density operators. By combining them, we can apply the usual bootstrap argument to obtain the main result.
item.dc:creator: Sonae Hadama

item.title: Global weak solutions to nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equations in bounded domains under physical initial data
item.description: arXiv:2510.06656v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the global existence of weak solutions to a nonlinear kinetic Fokker--Planck equation with degenerate diffusion, under either inflow or partial absorption-reflection boundary conditions. The novelty of our approach lies in constructing solutions under solely the physical assumptions on the initial and boundary data, namely finite mass, kinetic energy, and entropy, with no additional regularity imposed. To overcome the lack of uniform ellipticity, we develop a compactness principle based on weighted Fisher information, which yields strong $L^1$ convergence of approximate solutions. This framework provides a robust existence theory under only the physically relevant conditions, and applies uniformly to both inflow and partial absorption-reflection boundary settings.
item.dc:creator: Young-Pil Choi, Sihyun Song

item.title: The doubling property of the elliptic measure, for elliptic operators with drifts satisfying an average diverging condition
item.description: arXiv:2511.12942v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show doubling of the elliptic measure corresponding to the operator with an elliptic principal term and a drift that diverges, on average on Whitney cubes, like the inverse distance to the boundary, with a small constant. Essentially a small Carleson constant assumption on the drift, this generalizes earlier results with the hypothesis of pointwise smallness of such a drift. This relates to recent perturbative results of rough Dirichlet solvability in domains with drifts or potentials that satisfy a Carleson measure condition, which have also been considered earlier by Hofmann-Lewis and Kenig-Pipher. While we work in 1-sided chord arc domains, these results are new even for the half-space. In the process, we also prove Hardy inequalities in such domains with Alhfors-David regular boundary, using a stopping time argument.
item.dc:creator: Aritro Pathak

item.title: Timelike curves: homotopies and domain of determinacy
item.description: arXiv:2602.03715v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies domains of determination of linear strictly hyperbolic second order operators $P$. For an open set $\mathcal O$, a set $Z$ is a domain of determination when the values of solutions of the differential equation $Pu=0$ are determined on $Z$ by their values in $\mathcal O$. Fritz John's global H\"olmgren theorem implies that points that can be reached by deformations of noncharacteristic hypersufaces with initial surface and boundaries in $\mathcal O$ belong to a domain of determination provided that local uniqueness holds at noncharacteristic surfaces. Using spacelike hypersurfaces yields sharp finite speed results whose domains of determination are described in terms of influence curves that never exceed the local speed of propagation. This paper studies deformations of noncharacteristic nonspacelike hypersurfaces. We prove that points reachable by (repeated) deformations by noncharacteristic nonspacelike hypersurfaces coincide exactly with the set of points reachable by (repeated) homotopies of timelike arcs whose initial curves and endpoints belong to $\mathcal O$. When the set $\mathcal O$ is a small neighborhood of a forward timelike arc connecting $a$ to $b$, a natural candidate for $Z$ is the intesection of the future of $a$ with the past of $b$. This candidate is exact for D'Alembert's equation. We prove that it is also exact when $a,b$ are points close together on a fixed timelike arc. The timelike homotopy criterion fuels the construction of surprising examples for which the domain of determination is strictly larger (resp. strictly smaller) than the future-intersect-past candidate.
item.dc:creator: J\'er\^ome Le Rousseau, Jeffrey B. Rauch

item.title: Linear Asymptotic Stability of the Smooth 1-Solitons for the Degasperis-Procesi Equation
item.description: arXiv:2604.03060v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the asymptotic stability of smooth 1-solitons in the Degasperis-Procesi (DP) equation. Such solutions necessarily exist on a non-zero background, and their spectral and orbital stability has previously been verified by Li, Liu & Wu and by Lafortune & Pelinovsky. Using the complete integrability of the DP equation to establish the strong spectral stability of smooth solitary waves, namely that the origin is the only eigenvalue of the associated linearized operator acting on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and that, moreover, in appropriate exponentially weighted spaces the non-zero spectrum for the linearized operator admits a spectral gap away from the imaginary axis. This spectral gap result {{is then}} upgraded to an exponential decay estimate on the semigroup associated with the linearized operator, establishing a linear asymptotic stability result in exponentially weighted spaces. Finally, we outline analytical challenges with extending our result to the nonlinear level.
item.dc:creator: Simon Deng, Mathew A. Johnson, St\'ephane Lafortune

item.title: Spectral inequalities for weighted $p$-Laplacians via Talenti symmetrization
item.description: arXiv:2605.29721v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the weighted $p$-Laplacian associated with a measure $\mu$ having a continuous positive density with respect to the Lebesgue measure on an open convex subset $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that Talenti's weighted P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} inequality---originally established for Lipschitz functions on $X$---extends to the weighted Sobolev space of functions vanishing on the relative boundary of an open set $\Omega\subset X$, defined as the closure of Lipschitz functions supported away from it. This yields Faber--Krahn-type inequalities for the first $(p,q)$-eigenvalue of the weighted Dirichlet $p$-Laplacian. We present several examples fitting this abstract framework, in which the isoperimetric sets are balls, half-spaces, or complements of balls.
item.dc:creator: Giulio Bartoli, Giorgio Saracco

item.title: Well-posedness of the weakly singular Burton-Miller equation for Helmholtz transmission problems
item.description: arXiv:2606.24492v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Although various boundary integral formulations are available for the Helmholtz transmission problem, the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is promising because it possesses favorable properties for numerical computation. This paper rigorously shows that the weakly singular Burton--Miller equation is well-posed. We establish bounded invertibility on $C(\Gamma)\times C(\Gamma)$ for $C^2$ boundaries by proving injectivity and applying the Fredholm alternative. For the prescribed analytic incident field, the integral equation further yields $u\in C^{1,\beta}(\Gamma)$ and $q\in C^{0,\beta}(\Gamma)$, for $0<\beta<1$. We also provide a proof that its fictitious eigenvalues are associated with an exterior Dirichlet problem and an interior impedance problem.
item.dc:creator: Yasuhiro Matsumoto

item.title: A Trichotomy for Modified Scattering Across the Yukawa-Coulomb Transition
item.description: arXiv:2607.02992v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the long-time asymptotics of the three-dimensional Hartree equation with Yukawa potential \[ V_\mu(x)=\frac{e^{-\mu|x|}}{|x|}, \qquad 0\leq\mu\leq1. \] The Coulomb case corresponds to $\mu=0$, while $\mu>0$ introduces the screening length $\mu^{-1}$. In the limit $\mu\to0$ and $t\to\infty$, the asymptotic behavior depends on the comparison between the observation scale $t$ and the screening length $\mu^{-1}$, equivalently on the parameter $\mu t$. This leads to three distinct asymptotic regimes, according as $\mu t\to0$, $\mu t\to L\in(0,\infty)$, or $\mu t\to\infty$, with different modified scattering phases in each case.
item.dc:creator: Yonggeun Cho, Jinyeop Lee

item.title: Sonic-supersonic jet flows from a straight two-dimensional nozzle with van der Waals equation of state
item.description: arXiv:2607.20203v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This article concerns sonic-supersonic jet flows issuing from a two-dimensional straight nozzle described by the steady compressible Euler system under the van der Waals equation of state. The flow state is prescribed at the nozzle exit, while the surrounding medium is assumed to be either a vacuum or a static atmosphere with lower pressure. When the flow reaches the sonic state at the nozzle exit, the governing equations become degenerate hyperbolic and the resulting jet flow problem can be formulated as a degenerate free boundary problem. The analysis is further complicated by singular behavior near the endpoints of the nozzle exit. By employing characteristic decompositions and suitable a priori estimates, we establish the global existence of locally Lipschitz continuous sonic-supersonic jet flows expanding into a vacuum. Moreover, in the presence of a static atmosphere with pressure lower than that at the nozzle exit, we prove the local existence of sonic-supersonic jet flows near the nozzle exit.
item.dc:creator: Anamika Pandey, T. Raja Sekhar

item.title: Non-uniqueness for the Complex Ginzburg-Landau Equation
item.description: arXiv:2609.08985v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that singularities of the three-dimensional cubic complex Ginzburg-Landau equation developing from smooth initial data can induce non-uniqueness of solutions after the time of blowup. The solutions we study start as backward self-similar solutions, and the source of the non-uniqueness is an unstable eigenvalue of the linearization around the forward self-similar profile generated by the singularity. We establish the existence of this eigenvalue, and hence the non-uniqueness, by a computer-assisted proof for specific values of the parameters in the equation. The work is in part motivated by similarities to conjectured behavior for the Navier-Stokes equation, with which the complex Ginzburg-Landau equation shares several important properties, such as an energy inequality and the scaling symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Joel Dahne, Vladim\'ir \v{S}ver\'ak

item.title: Interaction between nonlinear diffusion and mean curvature of a surface with initial discontinuities
item.description: arXiv:2609.14358v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the Cauchy problems for a class of nonlinear diffusion equations where each initial data is given by a characteristic function of an open set $\Omega$ in the whole Euclidean space. If the boundary $\partial\Omega$ is of class $C^2$ in a neighborhood of a point $x$ on it, then we extract the mean curvature of $\partial\Omega$ at $x$ from the initial diffusion at $x$. This corresponds to the author's previous result for the two-phase linear diffusion equation. Applications to some overdetermined problems for nonlinear diffusion equations are given.
item.dc:creator: Shigeru Sakaguchi

item.title: Boundedness of radial solutions to the parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the plane with subcritical mass
item.description: arXiv:2610.28230v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish uniform-in-time boundedness of radially symmetric global solutions to the two-dimensional parabolic-parabolic Keller--Segel system on the whole space with mass below $8\pi$. While global existence is known throughout this subcritical mass range, uniform-in-time boundedness has remained open. On bounded domains, the free energy method of Nagai, Senba and Yoshida (1997) yields both global existence and boundedness under the optimal mass condition. On the whole space, however, the corresponding estimates are not uniform in time due to the behavior of solutions at spatial infinity. Indeed, the free energy of self-similar solutions diverges to $-\infty$ as $t\to\infty$, preventing a direct application of this approach to establish boundedness. The key ingredients are new interior estimates controlling the localized free energy in terms of its dissipation, together with uniform-in-time exterior estimates exploiting radial symmetry.
item.dc:creator: Tatsuya Hosono

item.title: Sharp Quantitative Convergence of Compactly Supported Aggregation-Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2610.29000v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish the quantitative convergence of nonlinear aggregation-diffusion equations in dimension one, with sublinear attraction kernel and degenerate diffusion higher than quadratic. In these models, steady state is known to be the unique, compactly supported, and radial decreasing probability distribution. In this paper, we work with compactly supported densities in dimension one, we prove these solutions converge to the steady state exponentially fast.
item.dc:creator: Yunhong Deng

item.title: Saturation on compact manifolds via Stone-Weierstrass type theorem, and forced nonlinear PDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.29914v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider polynomial nonlinear PDEs on compact manifolds with finite-dimensional forcing terms. We provide necessary and sufficient conditions under which the forcing, through the nonlinear dynamics, attains a dense subspace on manifolds with and without boundary. Our key argument is Nachbin's theorem, which is an analogue of the well-known Stone-Weierstrass theorem in spaces of differentiable functions. As applications, we prove small-time approximate controllability by additive finite-dimensional controls, topological irreducibility, and almost sure unboundedness of Sobolev norms.
item.dc:creator: R\'emi Buffe, Alessandro Duca, Hugo Parada

item.title: Corner Regularity and Asymptotics for the Two-Dimensional Radiation Transport Equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.32732v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The regularity of solutions to the two-dimensional radiation transport equation plays a central role in understanding the behavior of scalar flux near geometric corners. In a previous study of Kaper's corner singularity problem, the physical transport kernel was decomposed into its principal inverse-distance singularity and a lower-order remainder, reducing the corner asymptotic analysis to the question of whether the scalar flux possesses sufficient continuity to justify differentiation of the associated singular potential. The required regularity, however, remained unresolved. In this paper, we establish a sharp modulus-of-continuity estimate for the scalar flux generated by the physical transport kernel and prove the estimate $\omega_{\phi}(h)=O\!\left(h\log(D/h)\right)$, which implies Dini continuity. This estimate yields absolute convergence of the fluctuation term arising in the differentiated principal potential and permits a rigorous differentiation formula for transport solutions. Using this regularity framework, we derive the fixed-angle asymptotic behavior of the scalar flux and its first derivatives near a rectangular corner. For every fixed interior ray, the gradient exhibits logarithmic growth, while the scalar flux admits an $r\log(1/r)$ correction with an explicitly identified coefficient determined by the corner values of the flux and source. The analysis shows that a rectangular corner does not generate a singularity stronger than the logarithmic first-derivative singularity already present in smooth-boundary transport theory. Numerical calculations on benchmark problems are consistent with the theoretical predictions. These results provide a rigorous resolution of the regularity issue underlying Kaper's corner singularity problem and establish a mathematical framework for corner asymptotics in two-dimensional radiation transport.
item.dc:creator: Dean Wang

item.title: On the optimal mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled to the Navier-Stokes equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.09160v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the mass threshold for the two-dimensional Keller-Segel system coupled with the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations. In the absence of fluid interaction, the classical Keller-Segel system admits a well-known $4\pi$-critical-mass dichotomy: for every suitably regular initial datum of total mass $m<4\pi$, the associated no-flux initial-boundary value problem admits a global bounded classical solution, whereas for $m>4\pi$, there exist smooth initial configurations of mass $m$ such that the associated solution blows up in finite or infinite time. For the fluid-coupled system, Winkler ({SIAM J. Math. Anal.}, 52:2041-2080, 2020) first established global generalized solvability under the condition $m<2\pi$ and posed an open question whether the fluid action may lower the critical blow-up mass to some value lying between $2\pi$ and $4\pi$. Based on numerical evidence, Bonilla and Guti\'errez-Santacreu ({J. Numer. Math.}, 32:175-212, 2024) later conjectured that the critical value is still $4\pi$. In the present work, we resolve this open problem and provide a rigorous mathematical proof to the conjecture, which indicates that the presence of the fluid does not alter the critical mass threshold, and the entire classical subcritical regime remains intact---every admissible initial datum with total mass $m<4\pi$ generates a unique global classical solution that is uniformly bounded in time. Our proof relies on the construction of a new quasi-energy inequality.
